steps.title: Why trading feels so intense
steps.text:
When money is on the line, your body reacts as if you're facing a threat. Stress hormones rise, your heart speeds up, and your brain pushes you to **act fast** instead of thinking clearly.

This happens to everyone, beginners and professionals alike. The goal isn't to feel nothing. It's to stop those feelings from making your decisions.

steps.title: Fear and greed
steps.text:
Two feelings drive most trading mistakes.

**Fear**: of losing, of being wrong, of missing out. It makes you exit good trades too early, or jump into a move you didn't plan for.

**Greed**: wanting more, faster. It makes you take trades that are too big, or skip your stop-loss.

Neither feeling is "bad". The trouble starts when they replace your plan.

steps.title: Losses hurt more than wins feel good
steps.text:
Psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky found that people typically feel a loss about **twice as strongly** as a gain of the same size. This is called **loss aversion**.

In trading it shows up in two classic mistakes: **holding losing trades** and hoping they come back, and **selling winners too early** to lock in the good feeling.

steps.question: You're in a losing trade and feel the urge to move your stop-loss further away "to give it room". What's most likely going on?
options: Loss aversion: you're trying to avoid the pain of taking the loss
The market has sent you a clear new signal
Moving stops is part of every good plan
Nothing: it's a purely logical decision
steps.explanation: Moving a stop further away mid-trade is usually loss aversion in action. It turns a small, planned loss into a bigger, unplanned one.

steps.title: Decide when you're calm
steps.text:
The best defence is to make your decisions **before** you enter, while you're calm: where you get in, where you get out if you're wrong (stop-loss), where you take profit, and how much you risk.

Then, during the trade, the plan decides, not your feelings. That's why every exercise in this app asks for a stop and a target **before** you place the trade.

steps.question: When is the best time to decide where your stop-loss goes?
options: Before you enter the trade, while you're calm
When you feel nervous about the trade
steps.explanation: Before entry, nothing is at stake yet, so you can think clearly. Once money is moving, emotions get a vote.

steps.title: Name it to tame it
steps.text:
Simply **noticing and naming** a feeling ("I'm anxious", "I'm excited", "I want to win this back") helps take the edge off it and gives you a moment to think.

Try a 5-second check before every trade: **How do I feel right now? Am I following my plan?**

points: Money triggers a **stress response** in everyone.
**Fear** and **greed** cause most mistakes when they replace the plan.
**Loss aversion**: losses feel about twice as strong as equal gains.
Decide entry, stop, target and size **while you're calm**.
Name the feeling, then check your plan.
